solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mean annuities following a crash

indicators.note: after a crash things lie scattered and jumbled, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone's pension income turns stingy after a stock market crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like the adjective for stingy, but it is the verb: to hint at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest or imply something indirectly, which is one sense of the verb mean.

clue.text: Lover one turned over to whip very quickly

indicators.note: something turned over ends up facing the other way, so the preceding pair of words is read backwards

blocks.note: a lover of something is a fan of it
the Roman numeral for one
a lash is a whip, or to whip

explanation.surface: An admirer flips over and is flogged with alarming speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a flash happens in an instant, an idiom for very quickly.

clue.text: Leans back to swallow large port

indicators.note: going back means running the opposite way, so the word for leans is read right to left
whatever swallows something takes it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: to tip is to lean over
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone tips their head back to gulp down a big glass of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts the drinker's reading, but it is a harbour town: Split, on Croatia's Adriatic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a major seaport in Croatia, so it is an example of a port town.

clue.text: Upset about wide HGVs avoiding large fine

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset thing is turned upside down, so the word after it reads backwards
the trucks steer clear of the size abbreviation, so that letter is dropped from them

blocks.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wide
HGVs are heavy goods vehicles, which the British call lorries (trucks)
the clothing-size abbreviation, here removed

explanation.surface: A driver fumes about wide trucks dodging a hefty penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' and 'fine' both suggest anger and punishment; fine is in fact the reassuring answer. An HGV is a heavy goods vehicle, i.e. a lorry or truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no worries means everything is all right, an informal equivalent of the reply fine.

clue.text: Reduction in size divides beer firm

indicators.note: a thing that divides another splits it apart by sitting in its middle

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
making a dent in something reduces it, as in a dent in savings

explanation.surface: A brewery's downsizing splits the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it describes pasta cooked to keep a little bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Al dente is the Italian cooking term for pasta or vegetables left slightly firm to the bite.

clue.text: Nurse is unable to secure hospital entrance

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast within, so one letter goes inside another word

blocks.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
can't means is unable
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A nurse cannot keep the hospital's front door locked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a doorway but is the verb en-TRANCE, to captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to charm and delight them, which is what the verb entrance means.

clue.text: A little heroin will get this going

definitions.text: A little heroin will get this going

blocks.note: H is slang for heroin
a little means a bit

explanation.surface: A warning that trying a small amount of a hard drug starts an addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter for heroin 'gets this going', i.e. starts it, followed by A BIT. The whole clue also describes how an addiction begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is an addiction, and a little heroin is exactly what starts a drug dependency.

clue.text: What's up with wine one's left in rush

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word for what runs backwards
the numeral for one has left, so it departs from the wine
with here means having inside, so the shortened wine sits within the other piece

blocks.note: Eh? is said when asking what
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
the Roman numeral for one, which is removed

explanation.surface: Someone asks what's going on as a fellow drinker hurries off, leaving the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurried speed, a synonym of the noun rush.

clue.text: Job: An obstacle for every young man

definitions.note: the answer names the person who does the job, not the job itself

blocks.note: a bar is an obstacle, as in a bar to progress
per means for every, as in ten per day
a son is a young man of the family

explanation.surface: A job application warns of a hurdle facing every young man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a barperson is someone whose job is serving drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Working as a barperson, serving drinks behind a pub bar, is an occupation, so the clue treats it as a job title.

clue.text: Article on medium that's beyond one's belief

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the article comes first
beyond means further along, so the abbreviation for medium follows the possessive

blocks.note: the definite article
one is I, so one's is I'S
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a spiritualist medium that the writer finds incredible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic who contacts spirits, but it is just the size letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is religious belief in the existence of a god or gods.

clue.text: Let everyone down after stripping off

indicators.note: stripping off takes away the outer layer, so only the inside letters of the word remain

blocks.note: all means everyone
the word down with its outside letters removed

explanation.surface: Undressing disappoints everybody watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let down' looks like one phrase meaning disappoint, but the definition is 'Let' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow something is to permit it, which is what let means as a verb.

clue.text: Avoid irritating sort hosting society do

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the abbreviation for society is put within the other pieces

blocks.note: to duck is to avoid, as in ducking a question
arse is British slang for an annoying, stupid person
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge a tiresome person who is throwing a society party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party, but it means a hairdo: the duck's arse was the 1950s greased-back style, also called a DA.
explanation.definitionFit: A duck's arse is a 1950s men's hairstyle, and do is informal for a hairstyle.

clue.text: Stuff to learn this evening?

indicators.note: to stuff things somewhere is to cram them in carelessly, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A student wonders what homework they must study tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun for material, but it is the verb, cramming the letters around. The question mark marks this evening as just one instance of later on.
explanation.definitionFit: Later on means at some subsequent time today, and this evening is one example of such a time.

clue.text: Classic way to keep the wrinkles at bay?

definitions.text: way to keep the wrinkles at bay

blocks.note: first meaning: timeless, never going out of date

blocks.clueFragment: way to keep the wrinkles at bay
blocks.note: second meaning, read as two words: to grow old more slowly

explanation.surface: A beauty ad promises a time-tested method for preventing wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into AGE LESS, an instruction for avoiding wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ageless seems untouched by time, as a classic work does, while 'age less' is the advice for staying smooth-skinned.

clue.text: Romantic feeling, possibly, about male all-star group

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one word goes round the abbreviation for male

blocks.note: sentient means able to feel, so feeling is a possible gloss
M is the abbreviation for male
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A romantic feeling, perhaps, for a man in a celebrity band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantic feeling' looks like one phrase, but 'Romantic' alone is the definition, a noun for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic is a person ruled by tender emotion, which is what a sentimentalist is.

clue.text: Foreign Legion medical officer's new term

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
MO is a medical officer, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: The French Foreign Legion's doctor has coined a new word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign Legion' reads as the French military unit, but 'Foreign' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression, a new term in the language.

clue.text: Attacks in city the reason girl won't answer door?

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles

blocks.clueFragment: the reason girl won't answer door?
blocks.note: she won't answer the door because she's out

explanation.surface: A city muggings story, with a girl too scared to open her door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attacks in city' suggests crime, but 'in' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to strike or verbally attack suddenly, so lashes out matches attacks as a verb.

clue.text: Women's group corral sailor, Spooner's said

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the start sounds of the two words change places

blocks.note: a pen is an animal enclosure like a corral, and hearty is an old word for a sailor; Spooner swaps their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A group of women round up a seaman and tell him something.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of PEN HEARTY gives HEN PARTY. A hen party is the British name for a bride's pre-wedding night out with friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen party is a celebration for women only, typically before a wedding, so it is a women's group.

clue.text: What Lord rubbed to aggravate Lady's complaint

definitions.text: What Lord rubbed to aggravate Lady's complaint

blocks.clueFragment: What Lord rubbed to aggravate Lady's complaint
blocks.note: surface reading: an aristocrat's massage annoys his wife, who complains
setter's reading: the complaint is an ailment, and the lord of the house has been rubbing a servant's joint

explanation.surface: A lord's massage of someone provokes his wife's grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: The complaint is medical, not a grumble: the lord was rubbing the maid's knee, which a jealous Lady would resent. Housemaid's knee is inflammation from kneeling to scrub floors.
explanation.definitionFit: Housemaid's knee is the common name for prepatellar bursitis, a medical complaint caused by long kneeling.

clue.text: Capital exchange needed by those selling fruits

indicators.note: exchanging the capital means swapping out the opening letter of a word for another

blocks.note: pedlars are travelling sellers of goods

explanation.surface: Street vendors need a currency exchange in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city, but it is the first letter. The clue does not say what replaces the P; the crossings show it is M.
explanation.definitionFit: Medlars are small brown fruits of a tree related to the apple, eaten when half-rotten.

clue.text: Drug abuse making tenor fashionable

indicators.note: making the tenor fashionable turns that one letter into a word, so the letter is replaced

blocks.note: an insult is verbal abuse
T is the abbreviation for tenor, here replaced
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Drug misuse lets a singer become trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug abuse' reads as one phrase; 'Drug' is the definition and 'abuse' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is a hormone given as a medicine for diabetes, so it is a drug.

clue.text: On rough seas, a bit of bravery humbles

indicators.note: just a bit of the word is used, namely its opening letter
rough water is churned up, so the letters of the following word are tossed about

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of bravery
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A storm at sea tests a sailor's courage and humbles them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the anagrammed seas after A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to lower them in dignity, so abases means humbles.

clue.text: More than fed up, but almost reluctant to retire?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
to retire is to go to bed, so the shortened word is put inside the word for bed

blocks.note: loath means reluctant; its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone tired of their job but not quite ready for retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' suggests weariness, but the definition means over-full: more than fed. Retiring means going to bed, so the word for reluctant, cut short, is put in BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloated means swollen from overeating, so someone bloated has had more than enough to eat.

clue.text: He knocks out second part of farewell letter

indicators.note: to knock something out is to replace it by force, so one piece takes over another's spot

blocks.note: taken as written
ta-ta is a casual goodbye; its second letter is the one replaced

explanation.surface: A man knocks out part two of a goodbye letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farewell letter' looks like one phrase, but 'letter' alone is the definition, a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Cried on cracking drink being carried away

indicators.note: cracking into something means breaking into it, so one word is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
wept means cried; on just continues the crying

explanation.surface: Someone sobbed when breaking down over drink before being taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be swept up is to be carried along by strong feeling, which is what being carried away means.

clue.text: When liberal university town upset city

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the preceding four pieces read in reverse

blocks.note: as means when, as in as I left
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
U is the abbreviation for university
T is an abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: A progressive college town is unsettled by the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma in the United States.

clue.text: A party with stomach-turning grin?

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle, so turning it means the inner letters of the word for grin are flipped round

blocks.note: a grin is a smile
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: A guest at a party wears a nauseating grin.
explanation.walkthrough: Party here also means a person, as in the guilty party, which makes the whole clue a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimeball is a repellent, oily person, someone whose sickly grin turns your stomach.

clue.text: Topless labourer, a Chippendales assistant?

indicators.note: topless means the head is gone, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a toiler is one who labours

explanation.surface: A shirtless workman helps out with a male strip show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chippendales are a troupe of male strippers; their assistant might oil their bodies, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is someone who applies oil, a fanciful job for a male strip troupe's helper.

clue.text: Dance music business expert backing hot property?

indicators.note: backing means coming behind, so the business qualification follows the other piece

blocks.note: SA is sex appeal, which makes someone hot property
an MBA holds a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A music industry expert supports a hot new act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music business' looks like one phrase, but 'Dance music' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a Brazilian dance, and the name is also used for the music played for it.

clue.text: Act run off that separates state and church?

indicators.note: off suggests something gone bad or out of kilter, so these letters are rearranged
something that separates two parts sits between them, so it goes inside the word for state

blocks.note: to state is to say
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A law run out to keep state and church apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separates state and church' evokes the constitutional principle, but 'church' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A church was traditionally a sanctuary, a place of refuge, so it is an example, flagged by the question mark.
